text:
Sam (marketing): Heads-up — we need a small, verifiable bench snapshot for the launch demo next Tuesday. Goal: believable latency/throughput numbers for 1:1 interactive demo (chat-style), plus a short repro package we can hand to press if asked.

Sam (marketing): Specifically asking for: p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec throughput, cold vs warm (no cache vs warmed KV), and one quantized variant (int8) + FP16 baseline. Raw logs + perf histogram + seed list please.

Daniel (eng-runtime): Can do a focused smoke run. Quick Qs: what exact model + context length? how many concurrent users / tokens per request for the demo path? and do you need end-to-end (app->api) numbers or only server-side token timing?

Sam (marketing): Model: redwood-2-small (the one in the demo config), context 1024. Demo path is short chat turns ~20 tokens average, single concurrent session for live demo but we'd like a 5-user throughput number for claims. Need server-side timings (token-level) and end-to-end coldstart numbers for promo.

Priya (eng-runtime): Ok. We'll run: FP16 baseline, then int8 quantized profile q4f16 (closest we have). Plan: 3 cold restarts (measure cold coldstart), then warm runs 10k tokens each with continuous batching disabled to mimic single-session interactivity. We'll capture token timing, kv cache hit rate, and GPU power profile.

Priya (eng-runtime): Quick snippet for the smoke command (will run in our repro CI):
```bash
./bench_run.sh --model redwood-2-small --context 1024 --mode single-session --tokens 10000 
  --quant fp16 
  && ./bench_run.sh --quant int8 --repeats 3
```
Include --dump-trace to upload raw traces to S3.

Daniel (eng-runtime): Note: int8 variant will have slightly different tokenization timing due to kernel paths; we should record exact docker image + kernel commit for provenance. I'll include a small manifest: docker tag, commit sha, CUDA/cuDNN, and quantization recipe id.

Riya (marketing): Important: webinar and press want a simple artifact bundle we can link: 1) short one-page summary (numbers + bullet methodology), 2) raw CSV histograms, 3) a reproducible script (the bench_run.sh), and 4) the seed list and sample payloads we used. Can you add a README with the exact commands so our comms folks can reproduce?

Priya (eng-runtime): Yep. We'll generate artifacts in s3://redwood-marketing/bench-snaps/3601234567-demo-snapshot/ with: summary.pdf, histograms.csv, repro.sh, seeds.txt, manifest.json, and raw-traces.tar.gz. We'll keep the run logs and the CI job link. Expect initial artifacts in ~24h (running now on dedicated dev pool).

Daniel (eng-runtime): Also: do you want heatmap slices by token position (start vs tail) and sample by prompt length? Those change p95 significantly. If you care, say yes and we'll include the heatmap.

Sam (marketing): Yes please include heatmap slices (short <32, medium 32-128, long 128-1024). Those will help the webinar narrative.

BenchBot: Artifact upload started: s3://redwood-marketing/bench-snaps/3601234567-demo-snapshot/ (upload in progress). Will post final link when done.

Daniel (eng-runtime): One more ask: can marketing commit to a single "claim" sentence? e.g., "p95 latency X ms for interactive chat (single session)" — we need to ensure the wording matches the test conditions (context length, warm/cold, tokenization). Otherwise legal will flag it.

Riya (marketing): We'll draft language and share here before public posting. We'll avoid absolute claims for coldstart.

Sam (marketing): Thanks team — if you can tag me when artifacts land I'll pull the summary and coordinate with comms. :thumbsup:
